source: Qudūrī — Intro to Qudūrī, class notes 2026-09-09

cards.front: What role does مُخْتَصَر القُدُورِي play for a student?
cards.back: The entry point into the Ḥanafī school of thought

cards.front: What is the stated purpose of مُخْتَصَر القُدُورِي?
cards.back: To present the relied-upon positions of the madhhab

cards.front: What does مُخْتَصَر القُدُورِي deliberately leave out, and what does that make it?
cards.back: It mentions no evidences — it is simply a manual of law

cards.meaning: linguistically — a definition by the word's ordinary language sense
technically — a definition by the term's specialist usage

cards.text: Scholars define a term two ways: {{c1::لُغَةً::linguistically}} and {{c2::اِصْطِلَاحًا::technically}}
For a definition to be sound it must be {{c1::مَانِع::excluding}} — excluding what does not belong — and {{c2::جَامِع::including}} — including everything that does

cards.meaning: preventive — a definition excludes whatever is not necessary to it
comprehensive — a definition includes everything necessary to it

cards.front: What does فِقْه mean لُغَةً?
cards.back: To understand and comprehend

cards.front: Who gave one of the first technical definitions of فِقْه, and what was it?
cards.back: Imām Abū Ḥanīfah — an individual knowing their rights and responsibilities

cards.text: Abū Ḥanīfah's definition of فِقْه: {{c1::مَعْرِفَةُ النَّفْسِ مَا لَهَا وَمَا عَلَيْهَا}}
cards.extra: an individual knowing their rights and responsibilities

cards.front: What is the problem with Abū Ḥanīfah's definition of فِقْه?
cards.back: It is very broad — it takes in ʿaqīdah and ādāb as well

cards.text: The refined definition of فِقْه: {{c1::الْعِلْمُ بِالْأَحْكَامِ الشَّرْعِيَّةِ}} {{c2::الْعَمَلِيَّةِ}} {{c3::الْمُكْتَسَبَةِ مِنْ أَدِلَّتِهَا التَّفْصِيلِيَّةِ}}
cards.extra: the knowledge of practical legal rulings derived from their detailed evidences

cards.front: Translate the refined definition of فِقْه.
cards.back: The knowledge of practical legal rulings derived from their detailed evidences

cards.front: In the definition of فِقْه, what do “the detailed evidences” refer to?
cards.back: The four sources of fiqh

cards.front: Name the four sources of فِقْه. (Q, S, I, Q)
cards.back: القُرْآن، السُّنَّة، الإِجْمَاع، القِيَاس

cards.meaning: scholarly consensus
analogical reasoning

cards.front: What does “practical legal rulings” mean in the definition of فِقْه?
cards.back: The laws related to a person's actions or conduct

cards.front: What does the refined definition of فِقْه exclude, and to which science does that belong?
cards.back: Knowledge related to the articles of faith — that is the subject of ʿaqīdah

cards.text: The three categories of فِقْه: {{c1::عِبَادَات}}, {{c2::مُعَامَلَات}}, and {{c3::جِنَايَات}}

cards.meaning: rules and regulations of worship and its related actions, such as purification
commercial and interpersonal law, and judicial matters — adjudication, court procedure, evidence
crimes, offences, and their penalties — criminal law

cards.front: Which categories of فِقْه does القُدُورِي cover?
cards.back: All three — عِبَادَات، مُعَامَلَات، جِنَايَات

cards.front: What does شَرِيعَة mean لُغَةً?
cards.back: A watering hole or drinking place — where a person or animal comes to drink

cards.front: What does شَرِيعَة mean اِصْطِلَاحًا?
cards.back: What Allah has legislated for His servants from the religion — Allah's revealed code

cards.front: What is the شَرِيعَة for?
cards.back: It is what we follow to be guided in this world and to attain salvation

cards.front: What does the شَرِيعَة include?
cards.back: Creed, ritual acts of worship, morals, ethics, and law

cards.text: {{c1::فِقْه}} and {{c2::شَرِيعَة}} are often used interchangeably, but {{c3::شَرِيعَة}} is far the broader of the two

cards.front: What does شَرِيعَة take in that فِقْه does not?
cards.back: Creed, morals, and ethics — فِقْه is confined to practical legal rulings

cards.front: From which verb does مَذْهَب derive, and what does it mean?
cards.back: ذَهَبَ / يَذْهَبُ — to go, or to take as a way

cards.front: Grammatically, what two things can مَذْهَب be?
cards.back: Either a ظَرْف مَكَانِي or a مَصْدَر

cards.front: What does مَذْهَب mean لُغَةً?
cards.back: A way, course, or manner of acting; an opinion on a particular case; a doctrine; the opinion one chooses to adopt

cards.front: What does مَذْهَب mean اِصْطِلَاحًا?
cards.back: A legal school, or legal school of thought

cards.text: A مَذْهَب is a non-formal association of jurists sharing loyalty to {{c1::a particular set of legal precepts}} and {{c2::a particular methodology of interpretation and of deriving law}}

cards.front: Name the four extant مَذَاهِب. (Ḥ, M, Sh, Ḥ)
cards.back: حَنَفِي، مَالِكِي، شَافِعِي، حَنْبَلِي

cards.front: After whom is each مَذْهَب named?
cards.back: A master-jurist — a مُجْتَهِد قَطْعِي — to whom a particular methodology of deriving law is attributed

cards.front: Were there ever more than four مَذَاهِب?
cards.back: Yes — there used to be many more; these four were codified, preserved, and survived

cards.meaning: one who performs ijtihād — the master-jurist a madhhab is named for

cards.front: What is اِجْتِهَاد?
cards.back: The effort made to derive law, which is not self-evident, from the primary sources

cards.front: What does اِجْتِهَاد require of the one performing it?
cards.back: A great deal of skill and expertise across many subject areas

cards.text: A مَذْهَب is both {{c1::a framework for interpreting and deriving law from the Qurʾān and Sunnah}} and {{c2::the body of law that comes out of that framework}}

cards.front: Does following the Ḥanafī madhhab mean holding every opinion of Imām Abū Ḥanīfah?
cards.back: No — it is following the scholarly tradition that developed over time by adhering to the methodology of the founders

cards.front: Is following a مَذْهَب an objective in itself?
cards.back: No — it is a means to follow the Qurʾān in a reliable, systematic, methodical, and coherent manner

cards.front: What is the ruling on following a مَذْهَب?
cards.back: Not technically wājib or farḍ, but very highly encouraged

cards.front: In what sense does the average person not have a مَذْهَب?
cards.back: Their madhhab is that of the imam they go to with their questions

cards.front: Why should a student choose a مَذْهَب once they begin studying?
cards.back: To develop coherence and internal consistency

cards.front: Historically, what determined which مَذْهَب a person followed?
cards.back: Schools developed in particular regions; people followed the one they had access to

cards.front: What is Imām Abū Ḥanīfah's full name?
cards.back: النُّعْمَان بْن ثَابِت بْن زُوطَى بْن مَاه التَّيْمِي الكُوفِي

cards.front: Which part of Abū Ḥanīfah's full name is the part to know?
cards.back: النُّعْمَان بْن ثَابِت — Nuʿmān ibn Thābit

cards.meaning: the greatest Imām — Abū Ḥanīfah's honorific title

cards.front: Where and in what year was Abū Ḥanīfah born?
cards.back: In Kufa, Iraq, in the year 80

cards.front: Where and in what year did Abū Ḥanīfah die?
cards.back: In Baghdad, in the year 150

cards.front: What is Abū Ḥanīfah's place among the four Imāms?
cards.back: He is the first of them

cards.front: On what grounds do some consider Abū Ḥanīfah a تَابِعِي?
cards.back: He may have seen Anas ibn Mālik RA as a child

cards.front: At whose command was Kufa founded?
cards.back: ʿUmar RA

cards.front: Whose legacy made Kufa a major centre of learning?
cards.back: Ibn Masʿūd and ʿAlī raḍiyallāhu ʿanhumā

cards.front: How does Kufa rank for the number of Companions who settled there?
cards.back: More settled there than in any city apart from Makkah and Madinah

cards.front: Which Companions are named as the most prominent of those associated with Kufa?
cards.back: ʿUmar RA, ʿAlī RA, and Ibn Masʿūd RA

cards.front: How did the school of Kufa come into being?
cards.back: Out of the body of fiqh understanding that developed among the Companions and scholars who settled there

cards.front: What was Abū Ḥanīfah's family trade, and what did he do in his youth?
cards.back: A family of traders — he spent time as a silk merchant

cards.front: Who recognised Abū Ḥanīfah's ability and redirected him to studying?
cards.back: Imām al-Shaʿbī

cards.front: What did al-Shaʿbī advise Abū Ḥanīfah to do?
cards.back: To start studying Islam and sitting with the scholars

cards.front: Which field did Abū Ḥanīfah excel in before turning to fiqh?
cards.back: Theology

cards.front: In what year, and at what age, did Abū Ḥanīfah turn to fiqh?
cards.back: In the year 102, aged 22

cards.front: Who was Abū Ḥanīfah's principal teacher in fiqh, and what was his position?
cards.back: Ḥammād ibn Abī Sulaymān — the chief jurist of Kufa

cards.front: For how long did Abū Ḥanīfah study with Ḥammād ibn Abī Sulaymān?
cards.back: 18 years

cards.front: What did Ḥammād permit Abū Ḥanīfah to do?
cards.back: Give legal rulings on his behalf

cards.front: What happened when Ḥammād died in the year 120?
cards.back: Abū Ḥanīfah was offered his position, and reluctantly accepted

cards.front: How many scholars is Abū Ḥanīfah said to have studied with?
cards.back: Over 4,000

cards.text: Abū Ḥanīfah's fiqh lineage: he studied with {{c1::حَمَّاد بْن أَبِي سُلَيْمَان}}, who learned from {{c2::إِبْرَاهِيم النَّخَعِي}}, who learned from {{c3::عَلْقَمَة بْن قَيْس النَّخَعِي}}, who learned from {{c4::ابْن مَسْعُود}}
cards.extra: Four links back to a Companion.

cards.front: How did the madhāhib begin?
cards.back: As geographic schools — the understanding of the different scholars and Ṣaḥābah in different cities

cards.text: School origins: the Ḥanafī from {{c1::the school of Kufa}}; the Mālikī from {{c2::the school of Madinah}}; the Ḥanbalī from {{c3::ahl al-ḥadīth in Basra}}

cards.front: On what legacy is the Shāfiʿī school built?
cards.back: Makkah, then Madinah and Kufa, then later the ḥadīth movement in Iraq

cards.front: When and where did the school of ahl al-ḥadīth develop?
cards.back: In the later half of the second century, in Basra

cards.front: What did ahl al-ḥadīth want to do with ijtihād and qiyās?
cards.back: Minimise them — not eliminate them

cards.front: For how long did Abū Ḥanīfah teach fiqh and give fatāwā?
cards.back: Thirty years

cards.front: What need did Abū Ḥanīfah recognise in the fiqh of his time?
cards.back: For a structured, systematic, organised approach that had not existed before

cards.front: What body did Abū Ḥanīfah form, and of how many?
cards.back: A committee of 40 jurists

cards.front: What was Abū Ḥanīfah's own role in the committee's daily debates?
cards.back: He would listen to the discussion, summarise it, then offer his own conclusions and opinions

cards.front: What was the committee's goal, and what happened when it could not be reached?
cards.back: Unanimity and consensus — where differences could not be reconciled, the differing opinions were recorded

cards.front: Over what period did the committee work, and to what extent?
cards.back: Thirty years, deciding thousands of issues

cards.front: Complete the famous statement about him: “You jurists are doctors and we are the pharmacists, and you are …”
cards.back: …a man who has got hold of both sides

cards.front: What did Abū Ḥanīfah refuse to do?
cards.back: Serve the rulers and sultans of his time

cards.front: What was the consequence of Abū Ḥanīfah's refusal to serve the rulers of his time?
cards.back: He was placed under house arrest near the end of his life

cards.front: Did house arrest stop Abū Ḥanīfah teaching?
cards.back: No — it did not prevent him from teaching others

cards.front: In which month did Abū Ḥanīfah die?
cards.back: Rajab

cards.front: What was the cause of Abū Ḥanīfah's death?
cards.back: Poison administered by prison guards, on the command of the Abbasid caliph Manṣūr

cards.front: How many times was Abū Ḥanīfah's funeral prayer performed, and by how many?
cards.back: Six times — more than 50,000 people prayed over him

cards.front: Name Abū Ḥanīfah's four main students. (Z, AY, M, H)
cards.back: زُفَر، أَبُو يُوسُف، مُحَمَّد، الحَسَن بْن زِيَاد

cards.front: What is Zufar's full name?
cards.back: زُفَر بْن الهُذَيْل

cards.front: In which two fields was Zufar a scholar?
cards.back: Both fiqh and ḥadīth

cards.front: In what three fields was Abū Yūsuf a specialist?
cards.back: Ḥadīth, tafsīr, and the history of the Arabs

cards.front: What is Muḥammad's full name?
cards.back: مُحَمَّد بْن الحَسَن الشَّيْبَانِي

cards.front: Which two students are called the pillars of the madhhab?
cards.back: Abū Yūsuf and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan

cards.front: With whom did Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan continue after Abū Ḥanīfah died?
cards.back: Abū Yūsuf

cards.front: Which of the four Imāms did Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan teach?
cards.back: Imām al-Shāfiʿī

cards.front: Which of Imām Mālik's works did Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan narrate?
cards.back: The Muwaṭṭaʾ

cards.meaning: an absolute mujtahid — one who derives law independently; Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan was one, though out of respect he attributed his work to Abū Ḥanīfah
the six books of Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan — considered the backbone of the madhhab

cards.front: Whose opinions did Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan compile in ظَاهِر الرِّوَايَة?
cards.back: The well-established opinions of Abū Ḥanīfah, his own, and Abū Yūsuf's

cards.text: Years studied with Abū Ḥanīfah — Zufar {{c1::over 20}}; Abū Yūsuf {{c2::over 17}}; Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan {{c3::2}}
cards.extra: Four similar durations sit in this section; holding them in one view is what keeps them apart.

cards.front: What is Imām al-Qudūrī's full name?
cards.back: أَبُو الحَسَن أَحْمَد بْن مُحَمَّد القُدُورِي

cards.front: In what year was Imām al-Qudūrī born?
cards.back: 973 (CE — see draft)

cards.front: In what year did Imām al-Qudūrī die?
cards.back: 1037 (CE — see draft)

cards.front: What is Imām al-Qudūrī's standing among Ḥanafī scholars?
cards.back: He is considered among the leading ones

cards.front: What does مُخْتَصَر mean, and what does that imply about مُخْتَصَر القُدُورِي?
cards.back: An abridgment — it is itself derived from much more comprehensive books

cards.text: فَرْض: {{c1::مَا ثَبَتَ بِدَلِيلٍ قَطْعِيٍّ}} {{c2::لَا شُبْهَةَ فِيهِ}}
cards.extra: That which is established by a definitive proof, in which there is no doubt.

cards.front: What is a فَرْض, in the Ḥanafī legal values?
cards.back: An act established by a definitive proof which is not open to interpretation

cards.front: What counts as a definitive proof for a فَرْض?
cards.back: A verse of the Qurʾān, or a mutawātir ḥadīth

cards.text: سُنَّة مُؤَكَّدَة: {{c1::مَا وَاظَبَ عَلَيْهِ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ}} {{c2::مَعَ تَرْكِهِ أَحْيَانًا}}
cards.extra: What the Prophet ﷺ persisted in, while leaving it on occasion.

cards.front: Translate the definition of سُنَّة مُؤَكَّدَة.
cards.back: What the Prophet ﷺ persisted in, while leaving it on occasion

cards.text: سُنَّة غَيْر مُؤَكَّدَة: {{c1::مَا فَعَلَهُ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ مَرَّةً}} {{c2::وَتَرَكَهُ أُخْرَى}}
cards.extra: What the Prophet ﷺ did at one time and left at another.

cards.front: Translate the definition of سُنَّة غَيْر مُؤَكَّدَة.
cards.back: What the Prophet ﷺ did at one time and left at another

cards.text: In a {{c1::مُؤَكَّدَة}} sunnah the Prophet ﷺ {{c2::persisted in it, leaving it only occasionally}}; in a {{c3::غَيْر مُؤَكَّدَة}} sunnah he {{c4::did it at times and left it at others}}
cards.extra: Both definitions mention doing and leaving — the difference is which one was the norm.

cards.meaning: to persist in, to do consistently — the word that makes a sunnah مُؤَكَّدَة

cards.front: What does طَهَارَة mean لُغَةً?
cards.back: Cleanliness
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.text: طَهَارَة اِصْطِلَاحًا: {{c1::النَّظَافَةُ عَنِ النَّجَاسَةِ}} {{c2::حَقِيقِيَّةً كَانَتْ أَوْ حُكْمِيَّةً}}
cards.extra: Cleanliness from impurity, whether that impurity be actual or ritual.
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.front: Translate the technical definition of طَهَارَة.
cards.back: Cleanliness from impurity, whether that impurity be actual or ritual
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.front: What does the technical definition of طَهَارَة tell us about نَجَاسَة?
cards.back: That it has two types — حَقِيقِيَّة and حُكْمِيَّة
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.meaning: “physical” impurity — an impure substance
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.meaning: ritual or legal impurity
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.text: نَجَاسَة is either {{c1::حَقِيقِيَّة::physical}} or {{c2::حُكْمِيَّة::ritual}}; the حُكْمِيَّة is either {{c3::الحَدَث الأَصْغَر}} or {{c4::الحَدَث الأَكْبَر}}
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.meaning: minor ritual impurity
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.meaning: major ritual impurity
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.text: الحَدَث الأَصْغَر is removed by {{c1::الوُضُوء}}; الحَدَث الأَكْبَر is removed by {{c2::الغُسْل}}
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.front: What is غَسْل (washing), by definition?
cards.back: Water touches the body in any way until it drips — even a single drop
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.front: What is مَسْح, by definition?
cards.back: A wet hand touches the area
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.text: {{c1::غَسْل}} (fatḥah) is the act of washing until water drips; {{c2::غُسْل}} (ḍammah) is the ritual bath that removes الحَدَث الأَكْبَر
cards.extra: Same three letters — only the vowel separates them.
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.text: {{c1::غَسْل}} requires water to reach the area until it drips; {{c2::مَسْح}} requires only that a wet hand touch it
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.front: From which verse are the obligatory acts of wuḍūʾ derived?
cards.back: آيَة الوُضُوء
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.front: How many obligatory acts of wuḍūʾ does the verse give?
cards.back: Four
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.text: The four فَرَائِض of wuḍūʾ: (1) {{c1::غَسْل الوَجْه}} (2) {{c2::غَسْل اليَدَيْن مَعَ المِرْفَقَيْن}} (3) {{c3::مَسْح رُبْع الرَّأْس}} (4) {{c4::غَسْل الرِّجْلَيْن مَعَ الكَعْبَيْن}}
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.front: How is the face defined for غَسْل الوَجْه?
cards.back: From the top of the forehead to the bottom of the chin, and from earlobe to earlobe
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.front: What does يَد mean on its own, and what does مَعَ المِرْفَقَيْن add?
cards.back: يَد means from fingertip to shoulder; the modifier restricts it to up to and including the elbow
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.front: How much of the head must be wiped, and which part?
cards.back: One quarter — the front part of the head
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.front: Which act of wuḍūʾ is مَسْح rather than غَسْل?
cards.back: Wiping the head — مَسْح رُبْع الرَّأْس
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.front: On what do Abū Ḥanīfah, Abū Yūsuf, and al-Shaybānī agree regarding the limits?
cards.back: That the elbows and the ankles are included
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.front: What happens to the wuḍūʾ if one of the four obligatory acts is missing?
cards.back: It does not count
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.text: The beard in wuḍūʾ: if it is thick enough that {{c1::the skin cannot be seen}}, then {{c2::wiping along the beard}} suffices; if {{c3::the skin can be seen}}, then {{c4::the skin itself must be made wet}}
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.front: What decides whether wiping the beard is enough in wuḍūʾ?
cards.back: Whether the skin underneath is visible through it
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.front: Which part of the face may be treated with مَسْح rather than غَسْل?
cards.back: A beard thick enough to hide the skin
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.text: The سُنَن مُؤَكَّدَة of wuḍūʾ (1–5): {{c1::washing the hands three times before the container}}; {{c2::mentioning the name of Allah}}; {{c3::the miswāk, before rinsing the mouth}}; {{c4::المَضْمَضَة — rinsing the mouth}}; {{c5::الاِسْتِنْشَاق — rinsing the nostrils}}
cards.extra: Nine in total; 6–9 on the companion card.
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.front: How many times are the hands washed before putting them into the container?
cards.back: Three
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.front: According to al-Qudūrī, in what circumstance is washing the hands before the container a sunnah?
cards.back: On waking from sleep
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.front: Why did washing the hands before putting them in the container matter in al-Qudūrī's time?
cards.back: There was no running water — wuḍūʾ was made from containers
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.front: Complete the ḥadīth's reason for washing the hands on waking: “…for you do not know …”
cards.back: …where your hand was during the night
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.front: What do the commentators say al-Qudūrī overlooked about washing the hands?
cards.back: He tied it to waking from sleep — but the sunnah mu'akkadah is to wash them three times whether waking or not
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.front: The commentators call washing the hands a سُنَّة مُؤَكَّدَة — what does that tell you about the Prophet's ﷺ practice?
cards.back: He persisted in it, leaving it only occasionally
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.front: What is said at the beginning of wuḍūʾ?
cards.back: The name of Allah — bismillāh
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.front: When is the miswāk used in wuḍūʾ, and for what?
cards.back: Before rinsing the mouth, to clean the teeth
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, class notes 2026-09-16

cards.text: The سُنَن مُؤَكَّدَة of wuḍūʾ (6–9): {{c1::wiping the ears, inside and out, after the head}}; {{c2::running the fingers through the beard — for men}}; {{c3::تَخْلِيل — running the fingers through each other and through the toes}}; {{c4::repeating each washing three times}}
cards.extra: Nine in total; 1–5 on the companion card.

cards.front: How many سُنَن مُؤَكَّدَة does wuḍūʾ have?
cards.back: Nine

cards.front: Must the miswāk sunnah be fulfilled with a miswāk?
cards.back: No — any utensil that can clean the teeth fulfils it

cards.meaning: rinsing the mouth
sniffing water up into the nostrils
blowing the water back out of the nostrils

cards.text: {{c1::الاِسْتِنْشَاق}} is sniffing the water {{c2::up}}; {{c3::الاِسْتِنْثَار}} is blowing it {{c4::back out}}

cards.front: Which parts of the ears are wiped, and when?
cards.back: Inside and outside, after wiping the head

cards.front: Which sunnah of wuḍūʾ applies only to men?
cards.back: Running the fingers through the beard

cards.meaning: running the fingers through each other, and through the toes

cards.front: What does al-Qudūrī classify the mustaḥabb actions of wuḍūʾ as?
cards.back: Sunnah غَيْر مُؤَكَّدَة — recommended and encouraged

cards.front: What is the preferred position on al-Qudūrī's mustaḥabb list?
cards.back: That it is an oversight — they should actually be sunnah مُؤَكَّدَة

cards.text: Of the mustaḥabb actions al-Qudūrī lists, the only one that really is {{c1::غَيْر مُؤَكَّدَة}} is {{c2::wiping the neck}}

The mustaḥabb actions of wuḍūʾ: {{c1::intending purification at the start}}; {{c2::wiping the whole head}}; {{c3::doing it in sequence}}; {{c4::beginning with the right}}; {{c5::doing it consecutively}}; {{c6::wiping the neck}}

cards.front: Why is intention not required for wuḍūʾ according to the Ḥanafīs?
cards.back: The ḥadīth on it is neither mutawātir nor mashhūr, so it cannot add to the Qurʾān's requirements — and the verse does not mention intention

cards.front: How unusual is the Ḥanafī position that intention is not required for wuḍūʾ?
cards.back: Quite unique to the Aḥnāf

cards.front: What does “consecutively” require in wuḍūʾ?
cards.back: No breaks in between — not so long that a limb dries before the next is washed

cards.front: Which part of the neck is wiped, according to the Aḥnāf?
cards.back: The sides

cards.front: Describe the method for wiping the whole head.
cards.back: Wet the hands; join the middle, ring and little fingers, keeping the other two apart; wipe front to back then back to front; wipe inside the ear with the index and outside with the thumb; wipe the sides of the neck with the backs of the hands

cards.meaning: the nullifiers of wuḍūʾ — what causes minor ritual impurity

cards.text: The نَوَاقِض of wuḍūʾ (1–4): {{c1::anything exiting the two passageways}}; {{c2::impurity that flows beyond its exit point}}; {{c3::vomit, if it is a mouthful}}; {{c4::deep sleep}}
cards.extra: Seven in total; 5–7 on the companion card.

cards.text: The نَوَاقِض of wuḍūʾ (5–7): {{c1::unconsciousness overcoming the intellect}}; {{c2::temporary insanity}}; {{c3::laughing out loud in a prayer with rukūʿ and sujūd}}
cards.extra: Seven in total; 1–4 on the companion card.

cards.front: How many نَوَاقِض of wuḍūʾ are listed?
cards.back: Seven

cards.front: What are “the two passageways”?
cards.back: The front and the back private parts

cards.front: Three conditions must hold for exiting impurity to nullify wuḍūʾ — what are they?
cards.back: It rises to the surface; it flows beyond the exit point; and it reaches a place the ruling of purification attaches to — anywhere on the body

cards.front: For the wuḍūʾ nullifier of impurity leaving the body, which impurities count?
cards.back: Blood, pus, or a mixture of the two

cards.front: Does an open cut nullify wuḍūʾ?
cards.back: Only if the blood actually comes out and flows — not merely by being open

cards.front: How much vomit nullifies wuḍūʾ?
cards.back: A mouthful — so much that it is hard to keep in

cards.front: Which kind of sleep nullifies wuḍūʾ?
cards.back: Deep sleep, not light sleep

cards.front: What postures of sleep nullify wuḍūʾ?
cards.back: Lying down, on one's side, or reclining on something that would let the person fall if it were removed

cards.front: What counts as unconsciousness overcoming the intellect?
cards.back: Fainting, or being in a coma

cards.front: What counts as temporary insanity, as a nullifier of wuḍūʾ?
cards.back: A manic episode, not being in one's senses, or being drunk

cards.front: In which prayers does laughing out loud nullify wuḍūʾ?
cards.back: Every prayer that has rukūʿ and sujūd

cards.front: How loud must laughter be to nullify wuḍūʾ?
cards.back: Loud enough that the person next to you can hear it

cards.front: What does غُسْل remove?
cards.back: Major ritual impurity — الحَدَث الأَكْبَر

cards.text: The فَرَائِض of غُسْل: {{c1::rinsing the entire mouth}}; {{c2::sniffing water up the nose until it burns}}; {{c3::washing the entire body}}

cards.front: How many فَرَائِض does غُسْل have?
cards.back: Three

cards.text: المَضْمَضَة and الاِسْتِنْشَاق are {{c1::sunnah}} in wuḍūʾ but {{c2::farḍ}} in غُسْل
cards.extra: The same two acts, different rulings in the two purifications.

cards.text: The سُنَن مُؤَكَّدَة of غُسْل, in order: {{c1::wash the hands and private parts}}; {{c2::remove any impurity on the body}}; {{c3::perform wuḍūʾ as for prayer, but without the feet}}; {{c4::pour water over the head and whole body three times}}; {{c5::move aside and wash the feet}}

cards.front: Which part of wuḍūʾ is left out when performing it during غُسْل?
cards.back: Washing the feet — they are washed at the end

cards.front: Why are the feet washed last, after moving aside?
cards.back: It comes from a time when there were no drains

cards.front: Must a woman undo her braids for غُسْل?
cards.back: No — provided the water reaches the roots of her hair

cards.meaning: undue difficulty — the principle exempting a woman from undoing her braids

cards.text: What makes غُسْل obligatory: {{c1::ejaculation with force and desire}}; {{c2::intercourse, even without ejaculation}}; {{c3::menstruation}}; {{c4::postnatal bleeding}}

cards.front: Does ejaculation require غُسْل for both men and women?
cards.back: Yes — when it comes out with force and desire

cards.front: Does intercourse without ejaculation require غُسْل?
cards.back: Yes

cards.front: Does pre-seminal fluid require غُسْل?
cards.back: No — it requires wuḍūʾ only; it is minor impurity

cards.front: What is وَدْي, and what does it require?
cards.back: A thick fluid often preceded by urine in a male, usually from a problem — it puts one in minor impurity, so wuḍūʾ only

cards.text: The times when غُسْل is a سُنَّة مُؤَكَّدَة: {{c1::Jumuʿah}}; {{c2::the two Eids}}; {{c3::entering iḥrām for ḥajj or ʿumrah}}; {{c4::the Day of ʿArafah, for the ḥujjāj}}

cards.front: Who is the Day of ʿArafah غُسْل a sunnah for?
cards.back: The ḥujjāj

cards.meaning: something the Prophet ﷺ did as a human being, rather than as an act of worship

cards.text: Of the sunnah categories, {{c1::<bdi>مُؤَكَّدَة</bdi>}} is what he ﷺ persisted in, {{c2::<bdi>غَيْر مُؤَكَّدَة</bdi>}} what he did at times and left at others, and {{c3::<bdi>زَائِدَة</bdi>}} what he did simply as a human being
cards.extra: Three categories, one scale of emphasis.

cards.front: Which Companion was known for following even the <bdi>سُنَن الزَّوَائِد</bdi>?
cards.back: Ibn ʿUmar — the narrator of the ḥadīth of the five pillars

cards.front: What is the primary means of achieving ritual purity?
cards.back: Water
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

cards.front: Which two questions does the section on water answer?
cards.back: Which water can be used for wuḍūʾ and ghusl, and which can remove impurity
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

cards.front: Why is the classification of water less pressing today?
cards.back: Municipal water systems
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

cards.text: The fuqahāʾ divide water into three: {{c1::<bdi>طَهُور</bdi> (ṭahūr)::pure and purifying}}, {{c2::<bdi>طَاهِر</bdi> (ṭāhir)::pure, not purifying}}, and {{c3::<bdi>نَجِس</bdi> (najis)::impure}}
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

cards.front: What separates <bdi>طَهُور</bdi> water from <bdi>طَاهِر</bdi> water?
cards.back: Whether it purifies — both are pure in themselves, but only <bdi>طَهُور</bdi> is <bdi>مُطَهِّر</bdi>
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

cards.meaning: water already used for wuḍūʾ or ghusl, and collected
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

cards.front: Which of the three types of water is <bdi>مَاء مُسْتَعْمَل</bdi>?
cards.back: <bdi>طَاهِر</bdi> — not impure, but it cannot be used for ṭahārah
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

cards.meaning: unqualified water — water called simply “water”, as against qualified water such as rose water
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

cards.front: What is the ruling on <bdi>مَاء مُطْلَق</bdi>?
cards.back: It is always <bdi>طَهُور</bdi>
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

cards.front: With which kind of water does al-Qudūrī open the discussion?
cards.back: <bdi>مَاء مُطْلَق</bdi> — unqualified water
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

cards.text: The <bdi>مَاء مُطْلَق</bdi> al-Qudūrī lists: {{c1::water from the sky — rain, snow}}; {{c2::rivers}}; {{c3::springs}}; {{c4::wells}}; {{c5::the sea}}
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

cards.front: When does water stop counting as water?
cards.back: When something else dominates it and takes it out of its nature (<bdi>طَبْع</bdi>)
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

cards.text: <bdi>طَبْع المَاء</bdi>, the nature of water, is its {{c1::<bdi>رِقَّة</bdi>}} (thinness) and its {{c2::<bdi>سَيَلَان</bdi>}} (flowing)
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

cards.text: <bdi>أَوْصَاف المَاء</bdi>, the qualities of water, are its {{c1::<bdi>طَعْم</bdi>}} (taste), {{c2::<bdi>لَوْن</bdi>}} (colour) and {{c3::<bdi>رِيح</bdi>}} (smell)
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

cards.meaning: mixed water — water with another substance in it
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

cards.text: Mixed water: if the substance is {{c1::pure (<bdi>طَاهِر</bdi>)}}, it turns on whether it is {{c2::solid or liquid}}; if it is {{c3::impure (<bdi>نَجِس</bdi>)}}, on whether the water is {{c4::flowing or standing}}, then on {{c5::its quantity}}
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

cards.text: Water mixed with a pure solid (<bdi>جَامِد</bdi>) is judged by its {{c1::<bdi>طَبْع</bdi> — thinness and flowing}}; with a pure liquid (<bdi>مَائِع</bdi>), by its {{c2::<bdi>أَوْصَاف</bdi> — taste, colour and smell}}
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

cards.front: How much may water mixed with a pure liquid change and remain usable?
cards.back: At least two of its three <bdi>أَوْصَاف</bdi> must remain — one may change, not more
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

cards.front: What is the ruling on flowing water (<bdi>جَارٍ</bdi>) into which najāsah falls?
cards.back: It remains usable
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

cards.front: What is the ruling on a small quantity (<bdi>قَلِيل</bdi>) of standing water (<bdi>رَاكِد</bdi>) into which najāsah falls?
cards.back: Unusable — even a single drop makes it najis
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

cards.front: What is the ruling on a large quantity (<bdi>كَثِير</bdi>) of standing water into which najāsah falls?
cards.back: It remains usable
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

cards.front: For the Aḥnāf, what counts as a large quantity of standing water?
cards.back: 10 × 10 arm-lengths (<bdi>ذِرَاع</bdi>) in area, deep enough that scooping water does not expose the ground
cards.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30
